brief.situation: You are the security analyst on call and a member of the change advisory board at Marlow Freight, a fictional logistics company. Change CHG-1182 is being implemented in tonight's maintenance window (22:00-23:30) so the payroll server PAY01 can send files to a new payroll vendor before Monday's payroll. At 22:20 the IDS alerts on scans of PAY01 from the internet.
handover: The firewall configuration lives in version control; every change is a numbered version.
The network engineer who made the change has gone off shift.
howItWorks: The console shows alerts, the change and firewall events as they arrive, and the assets at stake.
Each task takes your time: start it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
When you close the incident, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: how you knew the change was wrong, why you backed it out the way you did, and how the business still got its change.

parts.label: Wrong change
parts.criteria: Compares the implemented configuration (version control diff) with the approved change record before acting.
parts.modelAnswer: The record approved outbound 443 to the vendor; the v41-to-v42 diff showed inbound 443 and 3389 from anywhere to PAY01. The IDS scans matched.

parts.label: Backout
parts.criteria: Uses the approved backout plan inside the window (accepting its planned service restart), not an unapproved live edit; checks PAY01's logons for a compromise.
parts.modelAnswer: I restored version 41 per the backout plan; the inspection service restart and the dropped VPN sessions were in the plan and inside the window. A live hand edit would have been an unapproved change and left version control wrong. PAY01's log showed no outside logons.

parts.label: Still delivered
parts.criteria: Raises an emergency change for the corrected rule, implements and tests it in the window, informs stakeholders and updates the diagram and records.
parts.modelAnswer: CHG-1183 corrected the rule with a peer review; it was implemented as v43 and the vendor test passed before 23:30. The owner, change manager and vendor were told, and the diagram and both records were updated.

governed.headline: Good: the process did its job
governed.body: You compared what was done with what was approved, used the backout plan written for exactly this, and still delivered the business's change through an approved, reviewed emergency change inside the window.

scoring.modelReasoning: The change record approved outbound TCP 443 from PAY01 to the vendor's range; the version control diff shows v42 added an inbound allow from anywhere to PAY01 on 443 and 3389, which the IDS scans confirm. Execute the approved backout plan (restore v41) inside the window, accepting the planned inspection service restart; a live hand edit or deletion would be an unapproved change and leave version control wrong. Check PAY01's logons for an outside success. Tell the change manager, the owner and the vendor, request an emergency change for the corrected rule with a peer review, implement it as v43 when approved, run the vendor test before 23:30, and update the diagram and both records. The lesson: review the diff against the approved change before it goes live.
